prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right attorney depends on your case facts, injuries, and what you want (trial experience, quick settlement, aggressive discovery, etc.). I can’t browse current local listings, but here’s a practical way to find the best personal-injury/truck-accident lawyer in Dallas for your situation and what to do next.

How to pick the right truck-accident lawyer
- Relevant experience: look for attorneys who focus on commercial vehicle/trucking collisions and who understand FMCSA rules, driver logs, ELDs/black boxes, and trucking company liability.
- Trial and verdict experience: truck cases often involve large insurers and complex evidence — an attorney who has taken truck cases to verdict and handled depositions, reconstruction, and expert testimony is valuable.
- Track record: ask about settlements and verdicts in truck cases (size, facts, and outcomes).
- Resources and team: truck cases require investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical experts — make sure the firm has those resources or established experts.
- Credentials and recognition: peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell AV), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, or board certification (Texas Board of Legal Specialization — Civil Trial Law) are useful signals.
- Communication and fee structure: contingency fee, clear costs, who will handle the case day-to-day, and expected timelines.
- Local courtroom experience: familiarity with Dallas courts, judges, and defense firms matters.

Immediate steps to protect your claim
- Get medical care and save records.
- Report to police and obtain crash report number.
- Preserve evidence: photos of damage, scene, injuries; witness names/contacts.
- Preserve truck data: ask your lawyer to send a preservation/spoliation letter to the carrier immediately to preserve ELD data, black box, driver logs, maintenance records.
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers without counsel.

Important legal points
- Statute of limitations in Texas: generally 2 years from the date of injury for personal injury claims (there are exceptions — act quickly).
- Truck cases often involve multiple liable parties: driver, trucking company, vehicle owner, cargo loaders, maintenance providers, manufacturers.
- Insurance limits for trucks are often higher than car policies, but carriers are aggressive — choose counsel experienced with those insurers.

Questions to ask during free consultations
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- What were outcomes and typical settlement ranges for cases like mine?
- Do you work on contingency? What are your fees and expenses?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What experts will you use (accident reconstruction, medical, economic)?
- How long do you expect this case to take?

Where to find and vet Dallas attorneys
- Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral
- Texas Bar Association lawyer referral
- Online directories and rankings: Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Justia
- Check disciplinary history on the State Bar of Texas website
